content.text: Subscribe Tuesday, apr 14 67° © 2026 Cantata Media American Airlines To Hike Bag Fees As Fuel Crisis Worsens During Iran War American Airlines is the latest major carrier to hike bag fees amid sky-high fuel costs during the US-Israeli war on Iran. 04/13/2026 6:00 a.m. The airline said the higher checked bag prices will apply to tickets booked on or after Thursday, April 9. Travelers at the airport will now pay $50 for a first bag and $60 for a second bag on domestic or nearby international routes.For tickets purchased on or after Monday, May 18, flyers will pay $55 for a first checked bag and $65 for a second. Customers who prepay online or through American's app will receive a $5 discount.AAdvantage members, certain credit card holders, premium cabin passengers, and active-duty US military personnel will continue receiving free bags. "These changes are the result of the airline's continuing evaluation of pricing and in light of the current operating environment," American said in a statement on its website.JetBlue Airways was the first major airline to reveal higher bag fees due to rising fuel costs. Delta Air Lines, Southwest Airlines, and United Airlines soon followed with increased prices. The airlines' moves come as the Iran war continues to cause turmoil in global energy markets.Jet fuel prices have surged since the US and Israel first launched attacks on Iran on Saturday, Feb. 28. As part of its defense, Iran virtually closed the Strait of Hormuz, blocking shipments through the crucial energy corridor. Despite a two-week ceasefire touted by President Donald Trump, just two oil tankers, one of them Iranian, and a handful of bulk carriers have moved through the strait since the deal was reached, CNBC reported. More than 100 commercial vessels passed through the waterway each day before the war began. American also announced that Basic Economy passengers will have to pay to select seats and will no longer be eligible for complimentary or systemwide upgrades starting on May 18.
